About

The Modern Stoic exists for one reason: ancient philosophy is more useful for a demanding, distracted modern life than almost anything currently marketed as "self-improvement" — and most people have never been introduced to it properly.

What This Is

This is a place to learn Stoicism the way it was originally meant to be used: not as an academic subject, but as a practical toolkit for staying clear-headed, acting with integrity, and wasting less energy on things you can't control.

Every essay here connects one idea from a Stoic thinker — Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Seneca, and the school's founders — to something concrete you're likely dealing with right now: a hard decision, a difficult person, a fear you haven't named, a habit you can't break.

Who It's For

This is written for people who are fully inside their lives — building something, managing a career, raising a family, carrying real responsibility — and want a steadier way to think, not an escape from the noise. You don't need any background in philosophy. You just need to be willing to test these ideas against your own life.

The Approach

Three things guide everything published here:

History first. The ideas land harder when you understand where they came from and who actually lived by them, often under far harder circumstances than most of us will ever face.

Practical over theoretical. Every essay ends with something you can actually do — a question to sit with, a practice to try, a shift in how you approach a specific situation.

Honesty over performance. Stoicism is not about suppressing emotion or appearing unbothered. It's about feeling the right things, for the right reasons, without being ruled by reactions that don't serve you. That distinction matters, and it shows up throughout this blog.
